topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines its core learning objectives concerning cancer therapies.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address traditional cancer interventions—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with the major challenges of systemic toxicity and multidrug efflux resistance.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer cell vulnerabilities and genetic defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that capitalize on tumor-specific weaknesses, such as hormone dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Small-molecule kinase inhibitors and targeted therapy resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss targeting oncogene-addicted kinases with ATP-competitive inhibitors and analyzing the structural, bypass, and paradoxical resistance mechanisms that subsequently evolve.

topics.label: Targeted monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine engineered antibodies directed against cancer cell surface antigens, both as receptor-blocking agents and as delivery systems for targeted cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell-directed therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the biological basis for antitumor immunity and explore therapeutic methods for activating or engineering T cells to destroy tumor cells.

topics.label: Overall progress, clinical challenges, and future directions in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesise historical treatment trends, persistent hurdles such as tumor heterogeneity, and emerging paradigms for future clinical cancer care.
